cleared.check: Site A, the exact-input fee mulDiv (src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:64-65, PoolManager pcs 22445 and 22513), never run with a product of 2^256 or more by the MegaETH and HyperEVM producers inside the PoolManager. Entry condition, cost, whether the call completes, and every place the word goes.
cleared.result: Entry: amountSpecified < 0 and |amountRemaining| * (1e6 - fee) >= 2^256, that is |amountRemaining| >= 2^236.068 at fee 0 and 2^236.073 at fee 3000 (python3). Hooks.beforeSwap returns amountSpecified unchanged for a hookless pool (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:252-253) and nothing bounds its size before Pool.swap. Any account reaches it in any existing pool with liquidity: the step aims at the next tick or the price limit, the amount consumed is only amountIn + feeAmount of the steps up to the limit (src/libraries/Pool.sol:379), and the settled amount (params.amountSpecified - amountSpecifiedRemaining) passes the cast at Pool.sol:452-460. Cost: the tokens of an ordinary swap of a few ticks plus swap gas. The word amountRemainingLessFee is used in three places only: the comparison at SwapMath.sol:69, and in the else branch as amountIn (:77) and as the input of getNextSqrtPriceFromInput (:78-80). A wrong word that is still >= amountIn changes nothing, because the target branch takes amountIn and feeAmount from getAmount0Delta or getAmount1Delta and mulDivRoundingUp (:66-74). A wrong word below amountIn sends the step into the else branch, where feeAmount = |amountRemaining| - amountIn (:82), so the step consumes the whole remaining amount, amountSpecifiedRemaining becomes 0 at Pool.sol:379 and (amountSpecified - 0).toInt128() at Pool.sol:455 or :459 reverts because |amountSpecified| >= 2^236. When the correct word is below amountIn (exhaust branch with a wide amount, which already reverts at the same cast), a wrong word above amountIn makes the step reach its target with the amountIn and fee that the price move costs (:69-74), which is the honest price for that move. No wrong word at this site raises amountOut, feeGrowthGlobal (Pool.sol:404-405, :446) or a delta the caller may take. Every wrong word ends in no change or in a revert.

cleared.check: Site C, the Position fee copy of mulDiv (src/libraries/Position.sol:93-96, pcs 22316 and 22378), never run wide by the MegaETH and HyperEVM producers inside the PoolManager.
cleared.result: Entry: (feeGrowthInsideX128 - feeGrowthInsideLastX128) * liquidity >= 2^256, which is the same as fees owed of 2^128 units or more in one currency, since the result is the product divided by 2^128. Fee growth only rises by fees and donations actually paid in: UnsafeMath.simpleMulDiv(feeAmount, Q128, liquidity) per swap step (src/libraries/Pool.sol:404-405) and simpleMulDiv(amount, Q128, liquidity) per donate (Pool.sol:473-478), and a position earns at most its share of them, so the operand needs 2^128 or more units of one currency paid as fees through one position. That is 3.4e38 base units; whether any asset other pools hold has such a supply was not checked (token sweep out of focus), and a token the account mints itself gets there. The conclusion below does not depend on which token it is. With the correct word the call always reverts, because feesOwed >= 2^128 fails feesOwed.toInt128() at Pool.sol:192. A wrong word above 2^127 reverts at the same cast. A wrong word below 2^127 credits that many units through feeDelta (Pool.sol:192) and callerDelta (src/PoolManager.sol:171, :183), but in the currency in which the account itself paid at least 2^128 units of fees, so the credit is smaller than what that pool received in that currency. The other currency has its own mulDiv with its own narrow operands (Position.sol:95-96). Every wrong word ends in a revert or in a loss for the caller.

cleared.check: Site D, the copies for an amount above uint160 (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:97, pcs 22721 and 22763, and :105, pc 20958), never run by either closed producer.
cleared.result: getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount1RoundingDown takes the mulDiv path only when amount > 2^160-1 (SqrtPriceMath.sol:95-97 and :103-105). It is called from getNextSqrtPriceFromInput in the exhaust branch of an exact-input step (SwapMath.sol:77-80), where the step then consumes the whole remaining amount (:82), and from getNextSqrtPriceFromOutput in the capped branch of an exact-output step (SwapMath.sol:96-98), where amountOut = amountRemaining and the step uses the whole remaining output. In both cases amountSpecifiedRemaining becomes 0 (Pool.sol:373 or :379) and the cast of amountSpecified - 0, more than 2^160 in size, reverts at Pool.sol:455 or :459. A wrong price word cannot avoid that cast, so every wrong word at these sites ends in a revert.

cleared.check: SqrtPriceMath.sol:52, the fallback divRoundingUp of the amount0 add path (pcs 23924 and 23928), which the censuses of cycles 33 and 37 show never executed on MegaETH or HyperEVM.
cleared.result: The fallback runs when amount * sqrtPX96 overflows or numerator1 + product overflows (SqrtPriceMath.sol:42-49), in the exhaust branch of an exact-input zeroForOne step. The exhaust branch needs amountIn to the target above amountRemainingLessFee, about L*2^96/target > 2^256/sqrtP, so with L <= 2^128 the step must span a sqrt price ratio of 2^32 or more, and the remaining amount must stay below 2^127 for the cast at Pool.sol:459, which forces sqrtP >= 2^129. The range then holds at least about 2^96 units of currency1 and the input is at least 2^127 units of currency0. Neither is payable in an asset others hold, so the account must use its own tokens on both sides, and a wrong next price there moves only the account's own tokens. Recorded as caller-only.

cleared.check: Fee growth update in the swap loop (src/libraries/Pool.sol:400-407) uses UnsafeMath.simpleMulDiv without overflow check; can feeAmount * 2^128 wrap in a swap that completes?
cleared.result: No. In every completing swap the settled input amountSpecified - amountSpecifiedRemaining passes toInt128 (Pool.sol:452-460), and each step adds amountIn + feeAmount to it (Pool.sol:379, or :375 for exact output), so feeAmount < 2^127 and feeAmount * 2^128 < 2^255. Larger fees only arise in steps that consume the whole remaining amount, and those swaps revert at the cast. The same bound holds for donate (Pool.sol:471-478), where amount0 and amount1 pass toInt128 first. The swap copy runs on both closed producers (pc 20231: 120,548 runs on MegaETH, 2,710 on HyperEVM, cycle 33 out/pm-sites.json).

cleared.check: Does this theme (PoolManager code that a block producer whose code differs from what eth_call runs has never executed) apply to the other 18 networks?
cleared.result: No. The cycle 39 plan scopes the theme to the three networks whose block producer runs code that is not what eth_call runs or that cannot be read: MegaETH's closed compiler-based executor, HyperEVM's closed validator and Monad's native compiled code. On the other 18 networks the code under test is the interpreter family that their endpoints run, which OPCODES.md covers with the battery, the script sets and mined swaps; the builds there that cannot be read (for example three of Arc's four builds and Elysium's) are open questions of other units, not of this one. The code readings of sites A to D above hold on every network, because they are about src/ only.

leads.question: Site B, the wide branch of getAmount1Delta (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:250-252, pcs 22585, 22639, 23094), has never run inside the PoolManager on the MegaETH or HyperEVM producer. Any account reaches it today in a hookless pool it creates from native currency0 and a currency1 that other pools hold (tick spacing 32767, price at tick 851,941, position [851942, 884709] with liquidity 2^96.5 costing 28,561,920,818 wei, exact-input oneForZero swap of 1000 units), and the result reaches the shared balance. Does the producer return the reference word there? The observation that closes it is one mined transaction through that site whose Swap log equals the reference (price after 249827439116968746553502782595956059949443474316 for the 1000 unit case) and which the MegaETH validator accepts and the HyperEVM replicas match on receipts root.
leads.why: The wide word (about 2^160) decides the comparison at SwapMath.sol:69 and must stay above amountRemainingLessFee. A word wrong by a factor of 2^33 or more downward (at most 2^127 instead of about 2^160) sends the step to its target at SwapMath.sol:71 for a payment of that word, crosses the upper tick (Pool.sol:413-431) and writes the price at Pool.sol:439. The position then claims getAmount1Delta(lower, upper, L), about 2^160 units of currency1 that the pool never received; burning it in slices of 1 liquidity, each a narrow product that computes correctly, yields about 1.31e19 units per slice through Pool.sol:230-235, callerDelta (src/PoolManager.sol:171, :183) and take (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297), which pays out the currency1 of every other pool and every ERC-6909 holder of that currency. The same wrong word at SwapMath.sol:102 (exact output of the position's token0) or at Pool.sol:222 and :232-234 (a mint whose correct amount1 is above 2^127 and reverts) gives the same claim. A wrong word above the correct one changes nothing. A MegaETH state-root mismatch would show the fault after the block; HyperEVM replicas would see the changed Swap log in the receipts root but compare no state root (F-120).

leads.question: Donate (src/libraries/Pool.sol:466-480, pcs 10223 to 10513) has never been mined through the PoolManager on MegaETH (0 Donate logs from block 7,009,653 to head) or HyperEVM (cycle 37 census, and this cycle's logs), and any account can call it today in any existing pool for 1 unit, for example donate(1, 1) in MegaETH pool 0x2ee008d1 (feeGrowthGlobal +50,899,744,793,315 per currency on the RPC nodes) or HyperEVM pool 0x10286777 (+394,266,451,089,267). Does the producer compute floor(amount * 2^128 / liquidity) there? The observation that closes it is one mined Donate whose fee growth word read afterwards equals the reference.
leads.why: A fee growth word that is too large is credited to every in-range position on its next modifyLiquidity through getFeeGrowthInside, Position.update (Position.sol:93-96) and feeDelta (Pool.sol:184-192), and is paid from the shared balance through src/PoolManager.sol:171, :183 and take at :291-297. An account that is the only in-range LP of a hookless pool of two shared currencies can donate 1 unit and collect whatever the wrong word credits. The operands are narrow (amount below 2^127 shifted by 128, divided by liquidity), the same shape as the swap copy at pc 20231 that both producers run, so a fault would need to be specific to the pc. Donate writes only storage and logs the amounts, so on HyperEVM a wrong word would show only when a later Transfer log differs; MegaETH's validator would see the state root.

leads.question: The exact-output branch (src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:88-104, getNextSqrtPriceFromOutput at SqrtPriceMath.sol:158-177 and the subtract paths at :101-118 and :53-72) has never run inside the PoolManager on the HyperEVM producer, and any account reaches it today with an exact-output swap of a few units in any existing pool, for example 1000 units in pool 0x10286777 (delta (1000, -3768879949) oneForZero on the official endpoint and both replicas). Does the producer return the reference price and amountIn? The observation that closes it is one mined exact-output swap whose Swap log equals the reference.
leads.why: In the capped branch amountOut is set to the remaining output (SwapMath.sol:96) whatever the price; the caller pays amountIn from getAmount0Delta or getAmount1Delta between the old price and the new one (:100-102) plus the fee (:104). A next price word that is too close to the current price, or an amountIn word that is too small, lets the caller take the full output from other LPs' liquidity while paying less, through amountCalculated (Pool.sol:375), the swap delta (Pool.sol:452-460) and take. This is the one never-run site that pays out of existing pools with real liquidity. MegaETH has mined it (174 runs at pc 19586) and Monad has run it in mined blocks and in the model.

leads.question: Replace the two OPCODES.md sentences that dismiss these sites. Proposed wording for the item at line 797: "PoolManager sites that the producers of HyperEVM and MegaETH have never run inside the PoolManager: the wide paths of four mulDiv copies, donate, the amount0 overflow fallback and, on HyperEVM, exact output. Cycle 39 traced every wrong word: the fee copy, the Position copy, the above-uint160 copies and the amount0 fallback can only revert or cost the caller, while a wrong word at the wide getAmount1Delta branch, at donate or on HyperEVM in exact output would pay out of the shared balance, and any account can reach those three today (getAmount1Delta for about 2.9e10 wei in a pool of its own from shared currencies, donate and exact output in existing pools). RPC nodes, replicas and pyevm return the reference words; no mined run inside the PoolManager exists, so the producers are untested there." Proposed wording for the item at line 799: "Three MULMOD sites of the PoolManager that MegaETH's producer has never run with a wide product inside the PoolManager. It has run that operand shape 495,303 times in other contracts in validated blocks. Two of them (the fee and Position copies) can only revert or cost the caller whatever they return; the getAmount1Delta copy is reachable by any account for about 2.9e10 wei in a pool it creates from shared currencies, settles with ordinary amounts, and a word too small by 2^33 there would pay out the shared balance of currency1."
leads.why: The current sentences say only a pool the attacker creates reaches them and a wide amount cannot be settled. Cycle 38 showed the fee site in existing pools with settleable amounts, and this cycle shows the getAmount1Delta site settles in an own pool of shared currencies and pays from the shared balance on a wrong word.

leads.question: Replay the Monad PoolManager transactions mined after block 125,760,000 with the cycle 30 classifier and list which of the 128 value-computing blocks (the 512-bit mulDiv paths, SqrtPriceMath large-amount paths, 100 percent fee path, donate) they entered.
leads.why: Monad's shipped emitter has run every one of these blocks on logged real states (cycles 31 to 37), and all validators run the same native code, so a compiler fault would be agreed by the quorum and seen only by an interpreter replay. leadResults.answer: Per site: the fee copy (SwapMath.sol:64-65), the Position copy (Position.sol:93-96), the above-uint160 copies (SqrtPriceMath.sol:97, :105) and the amount0 fallback (SqrtPriceMath.sol:52) can only revert or cost the caller whatever they return, by the lines given in cleared. The getAmount1Delta wide branch (SqrtPriceMath.sol:250-252) is reachable by any account in a hookless pool it creates from native currency0 and a shared currency1 for about 2.9e10 wei and 1000 units, completes with payable amounts, and a word too small by a factor of 2^33 or more at SwapMath.sol:69, :102 or Pool.sol:222/:232-234 would let the account claim about 2^160 units of currency1 from the shared balance through Pool.sol:230-235, PoolManager.sol:171-183 and take at :291-297. Donate (Pool.sol:473-478) reachable in existing pools for 1 unit pays a too large fee growth word out through Position.update and take. On HyperEVM exact output pays a too small amountIn or too close price out of existing pools. No result differs from the reference on any endpoint or in pyevm, so these are high-priority leads, not findings; the producers have never executed them inside the PoolManager.

These are RPC nodes, not the producer. The validated-block census of cycle 33 holds no wide run of the fee copy inside the PoolManager (pc 22513 never executed), and the swaps mined since its end were not validated in this cycle, so the producer has still never executed the branch inside the PoolManager. A wrong word there only reverts or changes nothing (cleared).
